details:
For certain use cases such as weapons or synced animations, I'd like to be able to specify a specific parameter/value for Contact Senders to set. If this parameter/value is omitted (or a checkbox not checked), the contact would simply send a bool True value as usual.

For the weapon example, a Contact Sender with tag "weapon" would be set to pass the value of a parameter called heldWeapon, which may have a value of 3. Another avatar with a hitbox capsule Contact Receiver would then be set to the same tag "weapon" and to set the parameter collidingWeapon to the value of a Contact Sender it collides with.

In this case, the first avatar's heldWeapon value is passed on to the second avatar's collidingWeapon parameter, and it would respond accordingly.

A second example for synced animations, one "broadcaster" avatar has a Contact Sender with tag "syncEmote" set to pass the VRCEmote parameter. Everyone with a compatible "syncEmote" contact/controller on their avatar within the broadcaster's range would then play the same animation. I've accomplished this with the current system by using 4 contact pairs to simulate a 4-bit number sync.

This could be used to a less "overpowering" degree to sync the colour of avatars as they get close to each other by syncing a float parameter, potentially lerping an existing float parameter toward the goal value by the contact's proximity, or averaging the float between all resolved contacts, though as more avatars enter the mix things may get complicated.

This might warrant a "multiple contact resolve method" option, for "first contact only" or "average all values", and a checkbox to lerp the value to its goal (though that may be achievable though other methods).

As usual for mismatched parameter types, they would be adapted as usual to the target type.

By the way, look at the absurd amount of contacts the SyncDances prefab adds. It'd be nice to see that cut back.
title: Contact-Based Parameter Sync Across Avatars
